# Trapezium

> A data table library for React, Vue, Svelte and plain JavaScript. Zero-config columns with type
> inference, per-column filters, global search, four pagination modes, selection, custom renderers,
> SSR, URL state and CSS-variable theming. No runtime dependencies.

Packages: @trapezium/react, @trapezium/vue, @trapezium/svelte, @trapezium/vanilla, @trapezium/core
Licence: MIT. Repository: https://github.com/Gregaly/trapezium

## Minimal usage

    import { Table } from "@trapezium/react"
    import "@trapezium/react/styles.css"

    <Table data={rows} />

Columns, headers, types, alignment, formatting, sorting, search and pagination are all inferred from
the data. Add configuration only to override a default.

## Common usage

    <Table
      data={rows}
      getRowId={(row) => row.id}
      search
      selection
      onSelectionChange={(ids, rows) => {}}
      export
      pagination={{ mode: "pages", pageSize: 25 }}
      format={{ locale: "en-AU", timeZone: "Australia/Sydney", currency: "AUD" }}
      columns={[
        { key: "reference", header: "Invoice", pin: "start" },
        { key: "customer.name", header: "Customer" },
        { key: "amount", type: "currency", filter: "range" },
        { key: "status", type: "badge", formatOptions: { options: STATUSES } },
        { key: "due_date", type: "date" },
        { key: "actions", header: "", sortable: false, render: ({ row }) => <Menu id={row.id} /> },
      ]}
    />

## Column definition

key (required, supports dotted paths and synthetic ids) · header · type · accessor(row) ·
format(ctx)=>string · formatOptions · render(ctx)=>node · renderHeader(ctx)=>node · sortable ·
compare(a,b) · searchable · filter · align · width · minWidth · maxWidth · pin("start"|"end") ·
hidden · resizable · reorderable · wrap · mono · icon · exportable · exportValue(ctx) · className ·
headerClassName · meta

`format` replaces the cell text and keeps sorting/filtering on the raw value.
`render` replaces the cell markup. CellContext = { value, row, rowIndex, rowId, column, text, format }.

## Types

text longText number currency percent boolean date datetime time relativeTime select badge tags
email url phone image id code address file json

Snake_case aliases accepted (long_text, multi_select→tags, timestamptz→datetime, money→currency,
uuid→id, jsonb→json, int8→number).

Custom type:

    defineType({ name: "rating", align: "end", format: (v) => "*".repeat(Number(v)),
                 normalise: (v) => Number(v), filter: "range" })
    <Table types={{ rating }} columns={[{ key: "stars", type: "rating" }]} />

`normalise` reduces a value to something orderable; sorting and filtering both use it.

## Filters

Kinds: text, set (checkbox list of values present in the data), range, date, boolean, none.
Operators: eq ne contains notContains startsWith endsWith gt gte lt lte between in notIn empty notEmpty.
A date filter written as a day matches the whole day. Empty cells satisfy no comparison. 0 and false
are not empty.

## Columns: moving and removing

Drag a header sideways to move it (a line shows the landing edge), drag a row in the column list, or
use "Move left"/"Move right" in the column panel. Drag a header out of the table to remove it, with a
puff of smoke; the last visible column refuses. All of it lands in state.order / state.hidden.
Disable with reorderable={false} on the table or a column. Pinned columns are not draggable.

## Pagination

pagination={{ mode: "pages" | "simple" | "loadMore" | "infinite", pageSize, pageSizeOptions, siblings }}
pagination={false} shows every row. Changing anything that affects matching rows resets to page 1.

## State

One serialisable object:

    { sort: [{key, direction}], filters: [{key, operator, value}], match: "all"|"any", search,
      page /* 1-based */, pageSize, selection: string[], order: string[], hidden: string[],
      widths: Record<string, number>, pinned: Record<string, "start"|"end">, density }

Controlled with `state` + `onStateChange`; uncontrolled with `defaultState`.
URL: stateToQueryString(state, { prefix?, include? }) and stateFromUrl(searchParams).
Saved views are JSON.stringify(state).

## Server-side data

    <Table data={page} total={total} server onStateChange={(state) => refetch(state)} />

In server mode nothing is filtered, sorted or paged by the table; `total` drives pagination.

## Server rendering

Renders completely on a server with the correct rows in the markup, no effects and no layout shift.
Formatting defaults (locale "en", timeZone "UTC") are fixed rather than read from the runtime, so a
server and a browser produce the same string. With `buildHref`, controls render as links and the
table works with no client JavaScript.

## Styling

CSS custom properties on `.tpz` (--tpz-surface, --tpz-muted, --tpz-border, --tpz-primary,
--tpz-row-height, --tpz-font-mono, …). Dark mode follows the page's color-scheme, or `.dark` /
[data-theme="dark"] on an ancestor, or theme="dark" on the table.
classNames={{ root, frame, toolbar, search, scroll, table, thead, tbody, headerRow, headerCell, row,
cell, selectCell, pagination, empty, loading, footer }} adds classes; `unstyled` drops the defaults.
responsive="cards" stacks rows below 40rem of container width, in pure CSS.
Bridge to shadcn/ui: import "@trapezium/react/themes/shadcn.css".

## Headless

`useTable(props)` returns { rows, rowIds, total, pageCount, filtered, columns, hiddenColumns,
allColumns, state, update, patch, types, format, pagination, selection, server }.
`@trapezium/core` has the whole engine with no renderer.

## Not included, on purpose

Grouping, aggregation, pivoting, tree data, formulas, Excel export. Inline editing and expandable
rows are planned but not in v1.
